newsitem.title: USA: Mild earthquake rattles Seattle; no damage seen.
newsitem.headline: Mild earthquake rattles Seattle; no damage seen.

text.p: A mild earthquake shook Seattle on Sunday, but there were no immediate reports of damage of injuries.
Media outlets and police fielded dozens of calls after the tremor hit about 11:30 p.m. EST. A police dispatcher said there had been no reports of any damage.

The quake registered 3.5 on the Richter scale and was centered three miles (5 km) southeast of Seattle, according to a preliminary report from the Pacific Northwest Seismographic Network at the University of Washington. It was followed about 15 minutes later by a smaller quake registering 2.0 on the Richter scale centered in the same location.
One woman who called a local television station said she felt a shaking sensation for more than 30 seconds in her 17th floor downtown apartment, but other callers said they barely felt the quake.
Earthquakes are fairly common in the Seattle area, where a tremor registering 2.3 on the Richter scale struck last week, centered about 25 miles (40 km) east of the city.
Last May a quake registering 5.3 on the Richter scale, the most powerful in three decades, caused minor damage and forced officials to halt a Major League Baseball game in progress.
